companies.label: Meituan
companies.metric_name: Core Local Commerce segment operating profit/loss
companies.metric_basis: Meituan's own disclosed Core Local Commerce segment operating profit/loss (food delivery + in-store/hotel/travel + instant-retail subsidy costs), as reported in quarterly HKEX results announcements
companies.latest_signal: Core local commerce swung from a RMB2.0bn operating loss in Q1 2026 back to a RMB5.7bn operating profit in Q2 2026 as delivery subsidy intensity eased from the Q3 2025 peak (-RMB14.1bn); on the August 2026 call management flagged that rival-driven in-store/hotel/travel subsidy competition could still pressure Q3-Q4 2026 margins even as the medium-term trend is improving.

companies.label: Alibaba
companies.metric_name: China e-commerce segment (Taobao/Tmall/Taobao Shangou/Ele.me) adjusted EBITA
companies.metric_basis: Alibaba's disclosed adjusted EBITA for its China e-commerce segment (renamed 'Alibaba E-commerce Group' from Aug 2026 after merging in AIDC and Freshippo); management explicitly attributes the YoY EBITA declines to Taobao Shangou/Ele.me instant-retail subsidy investment
companies.latest_signal: China e-commerce adjusted EBITA was down only 1% YoY in the June-2026 quarter versus -76% YoY at the Sept-2025 peak of the subsidy war; management says Taobao Shangou's unit economics are improving sequentially and the business has entered a 'loss-narrowing while growing' phase targeting UE breakeven by end-FY2027, but the segment was redefined in Aug 2026 to also include AIDC and Freshippo, muddying like-for-like comparison, and sell-side (e.g. CICC) estimates still put standalone Shangou EBITA losses in the tens of billions of RMB per quarter.

companies.label: JD.com
companies.metric_basis: JD's disclosed New Businesses segment operating loss (includes JD Takeaway/food delivery, Jingxi, overseas), as reported in quarterly SEC/HKEX results
companies.latest_signal: New Businesses operating loss narrowed for a fourth straight quarter to RMB9.85bn in Q2 2026 from RMB15.7bn at the Q3 2025 peak, helped by folding last-mile delivery capacity into the JD Logistics network to dilute marginal cost; CFO Sandy Xu has said 2026 full-year delivery investment will be lower than 2025's and that takeaway will 'ultimately be profitable.' Q3 2026 results are not out yet (due mid-Nov 2026); the Nov 4 2026 resignation of JD's local-services head (an ex-Meituan hire) is read by Chinese media (21jingji) as a signal the all-in subsidy phase is ending.

war_summary: The three platforms burned an estimated RMB150-220bn+ combined on delivery/instant-commerce subsidies from mid-2025 through Q1 2026, with competition peaking in Q3 2025 (Meituan's core local commerce swung to a RMB14.1bn quarterly operating loss; Alibaba's e-commerce EBITA fell 76% YoY). All three have shown sequential loss-narrowing since Q4 2025 as SAMR's draft anti-'involution' subsidy rules and investor pressure forced restraint: Meituan defended share and returned to a core profit in Q2 2026, Alibaba reframed Taobao Shangou/Ele.me as 'loss-narrowing while growing,' and JD settled into a ~15% share, steadily-shrinking-loss distant third. The November 2026 departure of JD's local-life business head is the clearest signal yet that the all-in subsidy phase is ending, though none of the three has committed to a full ceasefire on in-store/hotel subsidies heading into Q4 2026.
